items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Billy Eckstine, a lot of your name entertainers worked at this club... Billy Eckstine, all the really great voices, you know.

ctx.x: Can you tell us anything about your work with Joe Williams?

Yeah, you know like I met Joe way back, in fact I wish I had thought about it. There is a clipping I could have brought from Club DeLisa in Chicago. And it was Joe Williams “Stop Pretty Baby, Stop,” that song that he did. It’s a little clipping from Club DeLisa. I was working with, what was her name, Little Miss Cornshucks, I was working at the Club DeLisa with her. And there was just a whole, just a whole advertisement of Joe Williams and with whom he was working, you know, Red Saunders and so, but like I met…

morning about 5 AM Tuesday morning. I mean and I mean every club had something happening. You know so what would happen, I used to see Joe, he might be working at DeLisa and then he would probably go over to maybe over on 39th Street or to the Dusable Hotel or some of those different places and maybe do a gig or something. And you’d always, everybody would meet up at a certain place and have breakfast, and during those days the popular food was brains and eggs. Of course I know you wouldn’t think of that today.…
